body:
Fixes #8103.

Iterating over a literal sequence of one-character bytes literals inferred a C character item type, so the loop variable received integers instead of bytes objects:

```python
for c in [b'a', b'b']:
    ...
# c == 97, 98 instead of b'a', b'b'
```

Single-character `str` literals still iterate over `Py_UCS4`, which converts back to `str`.

This is split out of #8114 as suggested in review, to allow an independent decision about what change to apply to which legacy branches. The mixed item type part (e.g. `(123, 123.45)` or `[True, 2]`) remains in #8114.

New and updated tests are in `tests/run/type_inference.pyx` and `tests/run/for_in_iter.py`.

commit.message:
Keep single-character bytes literals as bytes objects when iterating

Iterating over a literal sequence of one-character bytes literals inferred
a C character item type, so the loop variable received integers instead of
bytes objects.  Single-character str literals still use Py_UCS4, which
converts back to str.

This is a separate change from the mixed sequence item type fix, to allow
independent decisions about backports.

commit.message:
Avoid stdlib distutils PATH races in Windows CI

Select setuptools' bundled distutils on Windows so concurrent MSVC
commands receive their own environment instead of mutating the global PATH

This fixes LNK1158 failures in the parallel shared utility memoryview test
with setuptools 59.8 on older Python versions

See https://github.com/pypa/setuptools/issues/2212

commit.message:
Generate refnanny C code before parallel benchmark builds

The bootstrap benchmark leaves refnanny.pyx for setuptools to translate
while the shared module changes global Cython options in another thread

Include the runtime source in the initial translation pass so the minimal
parallel build uses generated C files

See https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/7997
